hints.title: Catalog Universality Verification
hints.text: Identify customers whose distinct purchased product count equals the total number of products in the product catalog.

hints.title: Grouped Distinct Count Having Filter
hints.text: Group transactions by customer_id and compare count(distinct product_key) against a scalar subquery of total products.

hints.title: All Products Blueprint
hints.text: select customer_id from Customer group by customer_id having count(distinct product_key) = (select count(*) from Product).

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT customer_id
FROM Customer
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT product_key) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Product);
```

complexity.notes: Grouped distinct aggregation and single catalog count query run in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Joining customer with every product row creates a Cartesian comparison explosion.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Integer count equality check validates relational division in minimal memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT product_key) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Product).

import pandas as pd

def find_customers(customer: pd.DataFrame, product: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    total_prods = len(product)
    grouped = customer.groupby('customer_id')['product_key'].nunique().reset_index()
    res = grouped[grouped['product_key'] == total_prods]
    return res[['customer_id']]
